title: Elasticity matrix: hiring velocity vs bid-price experiment
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sheet to capture a compact set of scenarios that link hiring velocity (engineer & infra hires), GPU procurement strategy (reserved vs bid/spot), and front-line pricing experiments (per-token/embedding price tiers). Goal is to quantify short-term runway impact and unit economics sensitivity so product and pricing can coordinate an executable experiment for Q1.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Three hiring velocity profiles modeled across 12 months: Rapid (10 hires/mo), Steady (4 hires/mo), Pinch (1 hire/mo).
- Two GPU acquisition mixes: Reserved-first (75% reserved, 25% spot), Hybrid (50/50), Opportunistic (25% reserved, 75% spot).
- Pricing experiments: baseline price, -15% promotional tier, +10% premium tier for SLA-backed Dedicated customers.
- Primary metrics: monthly gross margin (USD), SLO hit rate, utilization, and runway delta (months).
- Key finding (preliminary): aggressive hiring paired with hybrid GPU mix improves feature velocity but increases burn; promotional pricing can increase utilization but only improves margin if spot mix stays below ~60%.

Assumptions (abbreviated - expand in linked model):
- Average fully-burdened cost per senior infra/serving hire: $28k/month in ramp year; mid-level: $18k/month; proportion in hires: 60% infra/platform, 40% eng-frontend/SDK.
- GPU unit economics: reserved GPU hour cost = $1.80/hr; spot/bid avg = $0.72/hr (with 18% preemption overhead -> effective cost 0.88/hr including reprovisioning ops).
- Throughput assumptions: 1 reserved GPU = baseline throughput X tokens/hr; quantized models (4-bit) improve throughput by ~1.8x at 6% quality delta.
- Baseline hosted API price: $0.00012 per token (generation). Embedding price baseline: $0.0008 per embedding unit.
- Demand elasticity approximations: price decrease -15% -> +23% request volume; price increase +10% -> -9% request volume (sensitivity differs by enterprise vs PLG).

Scenario tables (summary rows) - month 6 snapshot

1) Hiring velocity x GPU mix -> net burn / month (USD) and marginal throughput

Format: ScenarioName | Hires/mo | GPU mix (R:S) | Net burn/mo | Est. throughput delta | Runway impact (vs baseline)
Rapid-Hybrid | 10 | 50:50 | $1,250,000 | +42% | -3.1 months
Steady-Hybrid | 4 | 50:50 | $560,000 | +16% | -0.9 months
Pinch-Hybrid | 1 | 50:50 | $320,000 | +4% | +0.4 months
Rapid-Reserved | 10 | 75:25 | $1,430,000 | +40% | -3.7 months
Rapid-Opportunistic | 10 | 25:75 | $1,080,000 | +45% | -2.5 months

Notes on table: net burn includes hiring run-rate + incremental infra CAPEX/OPEX (GPU hours + reserved commitments amortized monthly) and incremental cloud network/storage. Throughput delta from added engineers (product + infra) and added GPUs estimated conservatively (engineer productivity curve applied).

2) Pricing sensitivity snapshot (month 6, Steady-Hybrid baseline)

Format: PriceTier | Price change | Volume delta | Gross margin per token | Net revenue change/mo
Baseline | 0% | 0% | $0.00008 | +$0
Promo-15 | -15% | +23% | $0.000055 | +$38,500 (volume-driven lift)
Premium+10 | +10% | -9% | $0.000088 | -$12,900

Interpretation: Promotional pricing increases throughput considerably and can contribute small net revenue lift in mid-range spot mixes; margin per token drops but utilization increases. Premium tier increases per-unit margin but can lower platform utilization, which exposes reserved-procured capacity and increases per-token amortized fixed costs.

3) GPU procurement experiment: breakpoint analysis

We model effective per-token compute cost across GPU mix and utilization. Breakpoint: when spot share > 60% and utilization > 75%, variance in preemption causes ~4-6% additional ops cost (retries + latency SLO penalties). Blended per-token compute cost sample:
- 75% reserved: $0.000020 per token compute cost
- 50% reserved: $0.000013 per token compute cost
- 25% reserved: $0.000010 per token compute cost (but add 0.000002 preemption overhead at high utilization)

Implication: pure spot is cheapest nominally but volatile; hybrid mix with active buffer (auto-reserved fallback) reduces SLO risk. For promotional pricing experiments we recommend hybrid or reserved-first to reduce loss from SLO-based refunds.

Open experiment plan (next steps for Q1 execution):
- Week 0: finalize the pricing cell test in product (control/promo/premium flags), create ticket JIRA-INF-2337 to wire up billing delta capture.
- Week 2-6: run promotional -15% in 10% of PLG traffic (A/B) with Hybrid GPU mix (50/50). Monitor: token volume, per-route latency P90/P99, cancellation/refund rate, and net revenue impact.
- Week 6-8: analyze results; if volume uplift >18% and SLO penalties <1.5% then expand promo window; otherwise revert.
- Parallel: procurement experiment to shift 15% additional capacity to spot for low-latency-background workloads (embeddings batch jobs) and measure preemption rate / requeue cost.

Quick sensitivity checks (notes/tradeoffs):
- Hiring: shifting 2 hires from infra -> product reduces short-term burn delta by ~7% but lowers throughput gains; tradeoff is longer ramp for tangible infra automation improvements.
- Pricing: enterprise customers show muted elasticity; can be trialed separately as premium tier without cross-subsidizing PLG promos.
- GPU mix: reserved commitments > 60% improves SLO and predictability but increases fixed monthly cost; negotiate flexible convertible reserved SKUs with cloud provider could reduce lock-in risk.

Data sources and model pointers:
- cost model: /contrib/cost-models/2025/hiring-and-gpu-blends.xlsx (linked in PR)
- user funnels: analytics://dashboards/hosted-api/usage-by-tier
- historical elasticity estimates: CONF-4902-2024-pricing-elasticity

Outstanding questions/assumptions to validate:
- True elasticity for embeddings (we assume same as generation; need to split in final model).
- Effect of quantization on perceived quality and potential churn for paying customers.
- Contractual implications of promo tiers for existing reserved/dedicated customers (legal review requested).

Action items (owner tags inline):
- Priya: finalize headcount mix per role and produce month-by-month P&L (due 2025-12-01).
- Ethan: create experiment config + billing capture (JIRA-INF-2337) and run initial A/B (due 2026-01-10).
- Laura: negotiate convertible reserved terms with cloud sales (note summary in linked_artifacts) (due 2026-01-20).

Notes to self (informal):
- This sheet intentionally conservative on productivity gains; infra automation can create step-changes but hard to schedule.
- Watch seasonal demand in Jan/Feb for PLG usage spikes — promotional experiments may confound natural seasonality.

Draft history:
- v0.1 2025-11-18 created (initial sketch)
- v0.2 2025-12-14 added GPU breakpoint numbers and sample net burn rows
- v0.3 2026-02-03 updated assumptions after infra team cost review
